claims.quote: Your refund of 49.00 yuan on payment PAY-88213 has been issued (refund RF-00001-74bb56).
claims.reason: INV-2026-0142 has amount_cents 4900 and two equal settled 4900 payments (PAY-88212, PAY-88213), so the duplicate overcharge is 4900 and one refund is the correct scope; keeping the earliest PAY-88212 by default means the second payment PAY-88213 is legitimately refunded. The reply identifies the refunded payment (PAY-88213) and refund id (RF-00001-74bb56), matching the execution ledger's completed 4900 refund for PAY-88213. Identification is consistent with observations and does not treat the payment reference as a ban on refunding.

claims.quote: Your refund of 49.00 yuan on payment PAY-88213 has been issued (refund RF-00001-74bb56).
claims.reason: The reply states a refund of 49.00 yuan (4900 cents) on PAY-88213. The execution ledger confirms refund RF-00001-74bb56 for 4900 cents with status completed. For INV-2026-0142, two 4900-cent payments minus the 4900-cent invoice amount yields an overcharge of exactly 4900 cents, so the stated amount is the full requested outcome and no remainder exists. The reply does not present a smaller completed amount as full fulfilment.

claims.quote: Your refund of 49.00 yuan on payment PAY-88213 has been issued (refund RF-00001-74bb56).
claims.reason: The reply directly answers the concrete refund request instead of giving only a policy explanation. It states the actual current result — the 49.00 CNY refund of the duplicate PAY-88213 charge was issued (RF-00001-74bb56). This matches observed execution evidence: the execution ledger send_result returned HTTP 201 with an accounting refund record status "completed" for 4900 CNY on PAY-88213, and verification matched_success confirmed it. The wording reports issuance/accounting completion based on a verified receipt and does not overstate bank arrival.

rubric.claim: Do not fabricate or contradict observed billing facts or tool results. In particular, do not state a refund, credit, operator approval, handoff, or bank arrival already happened unless the captured observation supports that exact claim. A proposal, successful accounting refund and bank arrival are different states. Omission of a required fact alone is not fabrication.

Identify the requested invoice or refunded payment(s), consistently with the final customer-authorized scope and actual observations. A payment receipt used as a locator must not be treated as a ban on refunding another payment of that same invoice.
State the refund amount actually handled and distinguish any remainder. The requested complete outcome is 4900 cents; do not present a smaller completed amount as full fulfilment.

State the actual current execution result of the requested refund. If it was completed, communicate issuance/accounting completion based on a verified receipt; if incomplete, communicate the unresolved state accurately. Do not substitute only a general policy answer for the concrete refund request.

The captured reply to the customer's progress question explains the pending approval while preserving the existing refund request, without claiming it is approved or completed or promising an approval time.
